verdict.rationale: The evidence describes Auth0 as the identity provider that authenticates users into a developer's own app (docs-1, docs-22, docs-43) or secures the developer's own API with OAuth (docs-2), and covers M2M/device flows (docs-8, docs-9) — all cases where Auth0 acts as the authorization server for the developer's app, not where the developer's app itself becomes an OAuth provider issuing tokens to other third-party clients ('Sign in with my app'). No evidence pack item mentions Auth0's third-party-application/dynamic client registration capability that would let a developer's app act as its own OAuth provider for external clients.
